message: A note block is an opaque cube, so the blocks beside it don't draw the faces that touch it: unless this model fills the whole block, those faces show through. A shape that isn't a cube wants "carrier": "leaves" (solid) or "tripwire" (no collision)
Tripwire breaks at once whatever the block's hardness: a tripwire block can't take longer to mine

Drawing tripwire blocks takes the game's own look of tripwire, which the editor writes into client/vanilla.json from your Minecraft: open the project in the editor with Minecraft 26.3 imported. Until then these blocks look like string
"otherpack:item/wing" is in no namespace the client has: name this pack's textures by their path under textures/ ("item/wing" for textures/item/wing.png), the game's with minecraft:
from is outside -16 to 32, which the game refuses to load (the whole model then draws as missing): scale the model down in its display, or split it into parts
"#1" is a texture this model doesn't give: add "1" to its textures
A rotation is { "origin": [x, y, z], "axis": "x", "y" or "z", "angle": degrees } or { "origin", "x", "y", "z" } in degrees
The game clamps a display's scale to ±4, so it won't be what this says: scale the centity node (or the model's elements) instead
"../wing.json" must be a .json path of letters, digits, _, - and . inside this resource pack's models/ folder
An item is drawn as one of a texture, a block and a model: it has texture and model
A block look is a model or textures, not both: the model's own textures are what it's drawn with
